# CD-PC on enwik8: a larger-corpus, restartable Colab experiment

**Default active runtime budget: 7.5 hours; one GPU.** Select **Runtime → Change runtime type → GPU**, then **Run all**. An A100/L4 is useful if available; the code also accommodates a T4. Throughput is measured on your assigned hardware. This is a time-budgeted experiment, not a promise of an exact finish time; fast hardware may finish earlier.

Everything needed is embedded in this notebook. Google Drive is the durable copy of the corpus, source, data splits, reader dictionary, feature caches, model/optimizer checkpoints, search trials and results. Computation uses local/GPU copies for speed. **Allow about 8–12 GB of free Drive space** to comfortably retain intermediate versions. Nothing in your run folder is automatically deleted.

## What this experiment tests

This scales the revised **Hybrid H2 / PC-CD v2** design. It trains a **7.56M-parameter byte transformer** from scratch, freezes it, and fits CD-PC and CD-BP caps on a new corpus. The original sandbox base had 120,576 parameters. The cap receives distributions from 13 transformer/suffix/copy readers; CD compresses the active graph to five readers while refitting.

| Question | Comparison |
|---|---|
| Does structural selection help? | Compressed CD-PC vs fixed-five PC, matched total optimizer updates including rejected trials |
| Does PC learning differ from BP? | CD-PC vs CD-BP; also fixed and full-bank PC/BP controls |
| Does prediction-time settling help? | CD-PC vs a separately trained no-inference gate on the same PC-selected graph; also frozen-gate interventions |
| What does compression cost? | Five-reader CD-PC vs all-13-reader PC |
| How much comes from memory alone? | Frozen transformer, a fitted global reader mixture, and a validation-selected single reader |

There are **three cap seeds and seven learned conditions (21 fits)**. Seeds share one pretrained base and dictionary. The notebook commits the common training budget before fitting these conditions. It does not change the recipe after seeing test results.

This is a test of the restricted hybrid architecture. It does not yet test an unrestricted STLM search guide, a jointly trained transformer/cap, or catastrophic forgetting across a task stream. All candidate-removal outcomes are retained for later search-guidance research.

CELL 1 markdown

## Corpus, protocol, and budget

[enwik8](https://mattmahoney.net/dc/textdata.html) is **100,000,000 bytes of Wikipedia text and markup**, about 90 times the Tiny Shakespeare file. The published MD5 is checked after download. It is used without text cleanup.

- First 90 MB: transformer training; first 16 MB also builds the fixed reader dictionary.
- Next 5 MB: separate halves for base-checkpoint selection and cap graph/checkpoint selection.
- Last 5 MB: held-out test region, accessed after model selection is locked. If time runs short, only completed conditions are evaluated and the report is explicitly marked partial.
- Cap fitting: **131,072 targets** in training blocks outside the dictionary prefix; 16,384 separate outcome targets and 16,384 validation targets.
- Test: **262,144 targets** spread over the held-out region. Each block has 256 bytes of input; the latter 128 positions are scored, with causal histories of 16 already observed targets.

These are **selected-block bpb scores**, not full-stream enwik8 leaderboard scores. The comparison remains paired across all methods. The report includes both test-region halves and descriptive paired block-bootstrap intervals.

Up to about **3.25 hours** are reserved for base training. The remaining budget covers dictionary/cache preparation, hardware-calibrated cap fitting and final evaluation. Cap update counts are common across arms, while elapsed times are recorded separately. Equal updates do not mean equal FLOPs.

The seven-hour-scale run has not been executed here. A smaller end-to-end enwik8 validation and checkpoint/causality tests accompany the source bundle. Colab GPU availability and limits vary; see the [Colab FAQ](https://research.google.com/colaboratory/faq.html).

import os, sys, time
from pathlib import Path

RUN_NAME = "enwik8_hybrid_v1"  # Keep this EXACTLY the same to resume.
TOTAL_BUDGET_HOURS = 7.5       # Includes recorded active time from previous sessions; maximum 8.

# The environment override below is solely for the supplied local notebook test.
LOCAL_NOTEBOOK_TEST = os.environ.get("CDPC_NOTEBOOK_SMOKE") == "1"
if LOCAL_NOTEBOOK_TEST:
    RUN_ROOT = Path(os.environ["CDPC_NOTEBOOK_TEST_ROOT"])
else:
    from google.colab import drive
    drive.mount('/content/drive')
    RUN_ROOT = Path('/content/drive/MyDrive/CDPC_Experiments') / RUN_NAME
RUN_ROOT.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
assert 0 < TOTAL_BUDGET_HOURS <= 8
print("Persistent run folder:", RUN_ROOT)
print("Resume by opening this same notebook and running all cells with the same RUN_NAME.")

# @title 3. Unpack the embedded, inspectable experiment code
import base64, gzip, hashlib, tempfile
WORK = Path(tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix="cdpc_notebook_"))
EMBEDDED = {
  "cdpc_experiment.py": "",
  "test_experiment.py": ""
}
EXPECTED_SHA256 = {
  "cdpc_experiment.py": "1e418d24a95bafe4c47868fbccd4128dd78db7c36c5b7fc7f9587e95f0645a8a",
  "test_experiment.py": "ffc2bc7505df6e6d5a6700a43b253bf138ad77c65e83bb3c32a91f01889362eb"
}
for name, packed in EMBEDDED.items():
    source = gzip.decompress(base64.b64decode(packed))
    assert hashlib.sha256(source).hexdigest() == EXPECTED_SHA256[name]
    (WORK / name).write_bytes(source)
sys.path.insert(0, str(WORK))
print("Plain Python source extracted to:", WORK)
print("The exact experiment source will also be saved in your Drive run folder.")

## Numerical and causal checks

The checks below verify the vectorized readers against an independent scalar calculation, causality under target/future edits, the energy derivative and weak-nudge gradient, nonoverlapping data roles, exact CPU continuation of the base and PC/BP optimizers, and fallback after deliberately corrupting the newest checkpoint in a temporary test directory. They never corrupt your experiment files.

## Run or resume

The next cell is the long-running cell. It prints progress roughly every 30 seconds during training, plus validation scores, data-cache progress, CD removals and checkpoint confirmations. The same messages are retained in `progress.jsonl` on Drive.

**To resume after disconnection:** reconnect to a GPU, mount Drive, and run all cells with the same `RUN_NAME` and unchanged notebook/configuration. The code verifies existing checkpoints and skips completed stages. The most recent uncheckpointed work may be repeated (up to roughly ten minutes of base training or two minutes of a gate fit). A manual interrupt retains the preceding complete checkpoint, avoiding a potentially half-finished optimizer update. CPU continuation is tested bitwise; changing GPU or PyTorch version can introduce ordinary floating-point differences.

The runtime budget counts recorded active execution across sessions, not the disconnected hours. If the budget is nearly exhausted, the notebook uses its evaluation reserve to report completed conditions where possible, explicitly marked as a partial experiment. Everything completed stays saved; missing comparisons are not presented as completed. The 7.5-hour setting can be increased to 8 when resuming, but changing model/data settings requires a new run folder. Network/Drive stalls and individual save operations can outlast a timing check; the notebook stops at safe boundaries rather than abandoning a write.

Do not run two copies against the same folder simultaneously. Keep previous folders: this notebook performs no automatic cleanup.

CONFIG = Config.smoke() if LOCAL_NOTEBOOK_TEST else Config(base_max_steps=300000, gate_factor_max=16)

print("Results directory:", RUN_ROOT / 'results')

## Inspect and return the results

The main metric is held-out **bits per byte (lower is better)**. Positive pairwise gain favors the first method. The three main contrasts are CD-PC vs fixed-five PC, CD-PC vs CD-BP, and CD-PC vs the retrained no-inference gate. The full reader bank is an accuracy reference, not a five-reader budget match.

A gain over the transformer alone does not isolate CD or PC: the dictionary contributes learned memory. Similarly, compressed graphs still share the dictionary and the reference cache materializes all readers, so reader count is not yet an end-to-end speed claim.

The bootstrap intervals describe this corpus's scored blocks; seeds do not provide independent pretraining or corpus replications. No learning or model selection uses final test scores.

## What is retained on Drive?

- `experiment_config.json`, `environment.json`, and `code/`: the fixed recipe and exact source.
- `data/`: original corpus/archive, checksum, split definitions, block positions and shared-memory accounting.
- `checkpoints/base_train/`: model, optimizer, mixed-precision scaler, RNG state, validation history and best weights; all committed versions are retained.
- Other `checkpoints/` folders: the frozen base, every dictionary depth, every feature-cache shard, global mixture, common cap plan, fitting states, CD candidate/control trials, final graphs and per-target evaluation losses.
- `progress.jsonl`, `setup_logs/`, and `results/`: ongoing progress, implementation checks, tables, comparisons, chart and compact return archive.

A checkpoint is visible to the loader only after its payload has been written and its hash verified, followed by a separate commit record. If the newest committed payload is damaged, the loader tries the preceding valid checkpoint. Incomplete temporary files are ignored and retained; there is no reliance on Drive reliably deleting them.

The final summary archive is deliberately small. It contains the report, recipe, environment, progress log, selected graphs/search outcomes and source; the larger model states, data caches and per-target losses stay in the Drive folder.

**Sources:** [enwik8 corpus and official checksums](https://mattmahoney.net/dc/textdata.html); [Colab limits and Drive guidance](https://research.google.com/colaboratory/faq.html). The architecture follows the accompanying *Generalized Transformers* synthesis and the revised H2 sandbox design.
